title: Augmentation height equals global dimension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] equipped with a commutative Hopf algebra structure. Explicitly, it has a coassociative $k$-algebra coproduct $\Delta:A\to A\otimes_k A$, a $k$-algebra counit $\varepsilon:A\to k$ with $(\varepsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\mathrm{id}$ under the tensor unit identifications, and a $k$-linear antipode $S$ such that $\mu(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=\mu(\mathrm{id}\otimes S)\Delta=u\varepsilon$, where $\mu$ is multiplication and $u:k\to A$ the structure map [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\ker\varepsilon)=\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No characteristic or reducedness assumption is made.

proof.text: Over an algebraically closed field, the weak Nullstellensatz (exists_algHom_ker_eq_of_isMaximal) writes each maximal ideal as ker(g). Define translation by g as the convolution of the structure-map composite of g with the identity. Associativity of convolution, its counit unit and the antipode inverse give mutually inverse algebra maps. In particular g composed with translation by its convolution inverse is the counit. The kernels therefore correspond under an algebra automorphism; RingEquiv.height_comap makes their heights equal. This is proved directly in the private translation helpers, without importing the downstream Cartier module or passing to group schemes.

The counit has proper kernel. Ideal.height_le_ringKrullDim_of_ne_top gives one inequality. For the other, apply ringKrullDim_le_iff_isMaximal_height_le and the height equality for every maximal ideal from step 1. This proves the algebraically closed case without a reducedness or characteristic hypothesis.

For arbitrary k, put K = AlgebraicClosure k, B = K tensor_k A and C = A tensor_k K. The tensor commutation equivalence identifies B with C. The algebra A -> C is integral by Algebra.IsIntegral.tensorProduct, since K/k is algebraic, and faithfully flat by Module.FaithfullyFlat.instTensorProduct. Thus its spectrum map is surjective and it has going down. The integral dimension inequality and the going-down/surjective dimension inequality give dim C = dim A. Finite-type scalar extension makes B finite type over the algebraically closed field K.

An integral algebra with going down preserves heights of primes: incomparability makes contraction strictly monotone, and going down lifts every strict prime inclusion below a given contraction. Order.height_eq_of_strictMono then gives equality of the two heights, equivalently contract and lift chains of each finite length. This is proved in height_under_eq_of_integral_of_goingDown and requires no Noetherian hypothesis.

Let P be the inverse image in C of the counit kernel in B under tensor commutation. It is prime. Its contraction to A is the original counit kernel: the composite counit on a tensor 1 tensor a is algebraMap k K applied to the original counit of a, and this field map is injective. Step 4 and invariance of height under ring equivalence give ht ker(counit_A) = ht ker(counit_B). Apply step 2 to B, then tensor-commutation invariance of ringKrullDim and step 3, to obtain the claimed equality.

mathlib_searches.query: The height of the augmentation ideal of a finite type commutative Hopf algebra equals its Krull dimension
For a finite type commutative Hopf algebra over any field, the height of the augmentation ideal equals the global Krull dimension

lean.statement: theorem height_ker_counit_eq_ringKrullDim (k A : Type*) [Field k] [CommRing A] [HopfAlgebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] : ((RingHom.ker (Bialgebra.counitAlgHom k A)).height : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim A
